chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The wergild (blood money) of the slave is his value. So if he was precious, the highest of his value would be ten thousand dirhams, and it does not exceed the wergild of the free man.

key_terms.دِيَةَ الْحُرِّ: The blood money of the free man
key_terms.دِيَةُ: Wergild or blood money paid for killing or injuring someone
key_terms.نَفِيساً: Precious, valuable, or of high quality

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum blood money for a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that while a slave's blood money is generally determined by their market value, there is a statutory cap of ten thousand dirhams for high-value slaves to prevent their compensation from exceeding that of a free man. This ruling reflects the juristic balance in Shia fiqh between the economic status of the individual and the inherent dignity of the human being, ensuring that the legal distinction between 'abd' (slave) and 'hur' (free) does not result in a disproportionate valuation of life.
